content.title: About
content.content: Ready-to-serve salsa is a flavorful tomato‑based sauce with peppers, onions and spices that requires no further cooking. It is perfect for dipping chips, topping tacos, meat dishes or vegetables. Salsa offers a fresh, slightly spicy taste and can range from mild to hot depending on the variety.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Salsa originates from Mexican cuisine and was traditionally made from fresh ingredients without cooking.
There are several types of salsa: salsa verde (green, made with tomatillos), red salsa (based on ripe tomatoes) and fruit‑infused versions with mango or pineapple.
Salsa is often considered a diet-friendly sauce because it is low in calories and fat.
Traditional salsa can be raw (pico de gallo) or cooked, which changes its texture and flavor.
In the United States salsa has become more popular than ketchup and frequently ranks among the top‑selling sauces.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Tomatoes and peppers in salsa provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system and helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes and other phytochemicals have antioxidant properties that promote heart health.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Salsa contains very few calories and virtually no fat, making it a good choice for weight management.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables aids digestion and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Peppers and onions supply vitamin B6 and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Spicy nature
items.content: Hot salsa can cause discomfort for people with sensitive stomachs, gastritis or acid reflux.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to tomatoes, peppers or the spices used in salsa.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Commercial salsas often contain added salt; those monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt versions.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain ready‑to‑serve products may include preservatives or sweeteners that are not suitable for all consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use salsa as a dip for chips, a topping for tacos, burritos, soups and salads, or as a marinade for meat and seafood. It also pairs well with grilled vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store opened ready‑to‑serve salsa in the refrigerator in a tightly sealed container and consume within 7‑10 days. Do not use if the lid is bulged or the product has an off smell.
